source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 5 (Land Resources and Agriculture).

sections.heading: 1. Land Use in India
points: Land use categories: **forest, land not available for cultivation, other uncultivated land (excluding fallow), fallow land, and net sown area**.
**Net sown area (NSA)** = actually cropped land; **gross cropped area** counts the area sown more than once.
**Cropping intensity** = (gross cropped area ÷ net sown area) × 100.
Forest cover is below the desired **33%**; **wastelands** are a concern.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Farming and Cropping Seasons
points: Farming: **subsistence, intensive, commercial, plantation**.
**Cropping seasons:** **Kharif (monsoon — rice, cotton, jute), Rabi (winter — wheat, gram, mustard), Zaid (summer — vegetables, melons)**.
Major crops: **rice, wheat, pulses, sugarcane, oilseeds, cotton, jute, tea, coffee**.

sections.heading: 3. Agricultural Development and the Green Revolution
points: The **Green Revolution (mid-1960s)** — HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation → self-sufficiency in foodgrains (mainly Punjab, Haryana, western UP).
**White Revolution (Operation Flood)** — milk; other 'revolutions' (blue = fish, yellow = oilseeds).
**Institutional support:** MSP, cooperatives, credit, land reforms.

sections.heading: 4. Problems of Indian Agriculture
points: **Dependence on the monsoon, small/fragmented holdings, low productivity, lack of irrigation, indebtedness, and land degradation**.
Environmental costs of the Green Revolution: falling water table, soil degradation, chemical overuse.
Need for **diversification, sustainable and organic farming, and better marketing**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Net sown area = actually cropped; cropping intensity = (GCA/NSA)×100.
Kharif (rice/cotton/jute), Rabi (wheat/gram), Zaid (summer vegetables).
Green Revolution (mid-1960s): HYV seeds → food self-sufficiency (Punjab/Haryana).
Revolutions: White (milk), Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds).
Problems: monsoon dependence, small holdings, low productivity, degradation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Cropping intensity = (gross cropped area ÷ net sown area) × 100**.
**Kharif = monsoon-sown; Rabi = winter-sown; Zaid = summer.**
The **Green Revolution** mainly benefited **Punjab, Haryana, western UP** (wheat/rice).
**White Revolution = milk (Operation Flood)**; Blue = fish.
